subject: tight ponytail
title: What If You Always Wore a Tight Ponytail?

scenes.text: What if you wore a tight ponytail every day? Your hairline would start moving back.
Day one, it might just hurt. In one study, 54 percent of women got ponytail headaches.
Loosening the hair fixed it, for most within thirty minutes.
After months of pulling, hairs snap along your forehead and temples. Doctors call it traction alopecia.
A clue: a thin fringe of short hairs left at the edge. It showed up in 85 percent of cases.
Caught early, it grows back. Keep pulling for years, and the follicles scar and quit for good.

description:
What if you always wore a tight ponytail? In a 2004 study, 54% of women reported headaches from ponytails, usually relieved within 30 minutes of letting the hair down.
Years of tight styles can cause traction alopecia along the hairline; dermatologists say it is reversible early but can become permanent scarring hair loss.
